Project: CARDINAL-DATA
Description: Extends the cardiovascular-renal-metabolic (CRM) data specification already proven in the London SDE. Builds on related work in the London SDE: the CARDINAL pan-London Driver Project (Hi Lab collaboration on CVD prevention, detection and treatment via VISOR, TRICORDER-PLUS and STAR-PULSE programmes) and the Boehringer Ingelheim Carepath Data+ initiative with Discover-NOW, which used linked primary/secondary care data for 228,000+ North West London patients to identify gaps in CRM care pathways.

Institution Hosting Project: London Secure Data Environment (SDE) / OneLondon

Project: TETHER (Trusted Environment Tooling for Health-data Exchange and Record-linkage)
Description: Prototypes automated data quality monitoring across the Scottish Safe Haven Network and stands up a data virtualisation layer for the first regional safe haven. Develops a reusable process for data ingest and data quality monitoring, pilots data flow from Public Health Scotland to one Regional Safe Haven, and improves data indexing and linkage across the Network.
Funding Award: HDRS Technology Transformation Projects - one of ten projects delivered by the Scottish Safe Haven Network receiving over £4.5m in total (RDS ~£1.36m; Scottish Safe Havens and wider ecosystem ~£3.14m)
Institution Hosting Project: Led by DataLoch; partners: RDS, DaSH, eDRIS, HIC, West of Scotland Safe Haven
Key People: ['Dr Melanie Ivarsson OBE (Chief Executive, HDRS)', 'Layla Robinson (Chief Operating Officer, RDS)']
Notes: One of ten Scottish Safe Haven Network projects sharing over £4.5m in total funding.

Project: Wessex SDE HRA Amendments as a National Exemplar
Description: Develops, tests and publishes a standardised HRA and CAG amendment route others can reuse. The Wessex SDE first obtained HRA approval in February 2024 (CAG Reference 24/CAG/0013) and provides annual returns to the HRA; amendments include adding National NHSE datasets (NCRAS, GP Prescribing; REC 01/09/25, CAG 10/11/25) and adding other SDEs as providers to link dementia data across five SDEs for the Connect-D study. One of five projects led by Wessex SDE (involved in 13 of 43 funded projects overall).
Funding Award: HDRS Technology Transformation Projects funding
Institution Hosting Project: Wessex Secure Data Environment (Wessex SDE; NHS-led, hosted at University Hospital Southampton)
Notes: One of five projects led by Wessex SDE, which is involved in 13 of 43 funded projects overall. First obtained HRA approval in February 2024 (CAG Reference 24/CAG/0013).

Project: Making secondary care medicines data research-ready (Med Map)
Description: Develops the standards and tooling needed to prepare hospital medicines data consistently in any secure data environment, tested on ePMA and high-cost drugs data within the NHS England SDE. Builds on dm+d, SNOMED CT, FHIR UK Core and Single National Formulary information architecture; centred on a Therapeutic Episode Model (computable record of a medicine with indication, dose, route, duration and outcomes). Launched October 2026; delivers by 31 March 2027.
Funding Award: Funded by the Health Data Research Service (HDRS) as part of its technical transformation programme
Institution Hosting Project: NHS England Secure Data Environment (lead); partners: Professional Record Standards Body (PRSB), University of Liverpool, Understanding Patient Data, King's College Hospital NHS Foundation Trust; supported by NICE, UK Biobank and Our Future Health
Notes: Launched October 2026; delivers by 31 March 2027. Centred on a Therapeutic Episode Model; tested on ePMA and high-cost drugs data within the NHS England SDE.

Project: STAR-Lab (Safe and Trustworthy Access to Pathology and Microbiology Free Text)
Description: Uses laboratory pathology and microbiology data to develop a standardised approach for de-identifying clinical free-text information, making it available for secure research. Evaluates Large Language Model (LLM)-based de-identification solutions across four Scottish Safe Havens, aiming for accuracy, scalability and preserved research utility while maintaining data safety and security. Active 1/10/26–31/10/27. Builds on the related DARE UK-funded STAR-TRE project (grant UKRI3005).
Funding Award: HDRS Technology Transformation Projects - one of ten Scottish Safe Haven Network projects receiving over £4.5m in total
Institution Hosting Project: Led by DataLoch (University of Edinburgh / NHS Lothian); partners: RDS, DaSH, HIC, West of Scotland Safe Haven
Notes: Active 1/10/26–31/10/27. Builds on the DARE UK-funded STAR-TRE project (grant UKRI3005). Dr Arlene Casey also holds a Versalius Senior Research Fellowship (PF2302/2) for related STAR-TRE work.

Project: RADIX on FHIR

Project: PRANA (Pre-hospital Research and Audit Network)
Description: Creates reusable pipelines and data dictionaries for onboarding ambulance, air ambulance and trauma data. PRANA is a secure national research platform hosted within the Wessex SDE, linking ambulance, hospital, police, registry and mortality data across the full patient pathway for research into pre-hospital care and road traffic collisions; has linked approximately 400,000 police and hospital records and is recognised in the Government's Road Safety Strategy. Two DfT-funded pilot projects focus on road traffic accident prevention and treatment.
Funding Award: Awarded funding through the HDRS Technical Transformation programme; pilot research projects funded by the Department for Transport (DfT)
Institution Hosting Project: Hosted within the Wessex Secure Data Environment (Wessex SDE); research partners: University of Leicester, University Hospitals Birmingham; supported by Air Ambulances UK and a network of NHS organisations, emergency services, government bodies, researchers and road safety organisations
Notes: Has linked approximately 400,000 police and hospital records and is recognised in the Government's Road Safety Strategy. Two DfT-funded pilot projects focus on road traffic accident prevention and treatment.

Project: NHS-accessible secure compute on national AI Research Resource infrastructure
Description: Builds a trusted research environment on national supercomputing capacity (the AI Research Resource, AIRR - including Dawn at Cambridge and Isambard-AI at Bristol), and works out the approvals and information governance route NHS data would need. Project: Pathfinding on OpenSAFELY tools in the NHS England National SDE
Description: Tests whether the OpenSAFELY ehrQL approach can prepare HES data for national SDE users. ehrQL is a Python-based query language for electronic health record data built by the OpenSAFELY team at the Bennett Institute for Applied Data Science, University of Oxford; a dedicated repository (ehrql-natsde-hes) exists for this work. OpenSAFELY operates across primary care records of >99% of England's population with NHS England support.

Description: Improves metadata coverage and quality across the Scottish Safe Haven Network so available data is easier to see.
